payload.title: Oceania Wedding Destinations From Fiji to Tahiti
payload.meta_title: Oceania Wedding Destinations From Fiji to Tahiti
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with AUD 150k or more to spend who want a wedding within a short flight of home, somewhere in the Pacific, New Zealand or on an Australian island, and who are weighing the places they already know (Fiji, New Zealand, Hawaii) against ones they have only seen on a friend's honeymoon feed (Tahiti, the Cook Islands, Samoa, Vanuatu), and who want to know plainly what each place is like for a wedding, when its wet or cyclone season falls, whether they can marry legally there or should plan a symbolic ceremony, and what to ask a venue before paying a deposit.
payload.goal: Book a consultation with a Wedded Advisor (Speak with a Wedded Advisor).
payload.angle: Most Pacific wedding lists are a scroll of overwater photos with every island sold the same way. The real differences that decide a wedding are the season and the paperwork: much of the tropical South Pacific has a cyclone season that official sources date, Hawaii sits north of the equator with its own wet winter, New Zealand has four seasons, and whether you can marry legally depends on each country's own rules, some of which are not published clearly for visitors. This page gives ten unranked places grouped by region (Melanesia, Polynesia, New Zealand and one Australian island entry), with seasons quoted only from the national weather service or WMO for a named station and period, cyclone lines dated from Smartraveller, legal or symbolic said only as an official source states it (otherwise 'check with the destination's authorities'), the trade-off said plainly, and two venue questions per place. It also says honestly which places we have a full guide for and which we do not yet.
must_include: Direct answer intro (2 to 3 sentences): Oceania for a wedding means the islands of Melanesia and Polynesia, New Zealand and Australia; the tropical islands share warm weather and a wet or cyclone season that official sources date, New Zealand has four seasons, and the legal route differs by country. Then exactly 4 one-sentence takeaways: (1) the ten places, unranked, in four groups from Fiji to Tahiti; (2) much of the tropical South Pacific has a cyclone season Smartraveller dates (Fiji's is November to April, quoted as at November 2026), so covered space and a buffer day belong in the plan; (3) whether you can marry legally differs by country, and where no official page states the steps the answer is to check with the destination's authorities or plan a symbolic ceremony; (4) we have full guides for Fiji, New Zealand, Hawaii and the Whitsundays, and the other entries are sourced from official pages only. Each takeaway is one sentence. Write fresh: no sentences reused from the month pages.

Short 'How we chose these Oceania destinations' section: unranked, grouped by region, seasons only from a national weather service or WMO page naming station and period, legal lines only from official sources, and a plain statement that some entries do not yet have a guide of ours. Include the WMO care-when-comparing remark if the batch confirms the page wording. LINK comment for the November destinations draft: <!-- LINK: /destination-weddings/wedding-destinations-november when live -->.

Group 'Melanesia' (3 entries, unranked): Fiji -> /destinations/oceania/fiji (our guide; optional second link /magazine/fiji/get-wedded-in-fiji if live); Vanuatu (no guide of ours, link none); New Caledonia (no guide of ours, link none). New Caledonia's Smartraveller advice level and any security line are quoted exactly as published and dated as at November 2026; no softening and no added commentary.

Group 'Polynesia' (5 entries, unranked): Tahiti and French Polynesia (no guide, link none); the Cook Islands (no guide, link none); Samoa (no guide; may link /a-traditional-samoan-wedding-celebration as cultural reading if live, and a LINK comment for /expert-advice/samoan-wedding-traditions, which is a draft); Tonga (no guide, link none); Hawaii -> /destination-weddings/getting-married-in-hawaii (our guide). Hawaii is said plainly to be north of the equator, a US state, with the October to April wetter winter NWS Honolulu describes (reuse November facts 113 and 114).

Group 'New Zealand' (1 entry): New Zealand -> /destination-weddings/get-married-in-new-zealand (our guide). Four seasons; temperate, not tropical; weather changes quickly as Smartraveller says (reuse November fact_104). Legal lines only from the New Zealand guide's pack (licence, celebrant), never restated beyond what that pack holds.

Group 'Australia' (1 entry): the Whitsundays and the Great Barrier Reef islands -> /everything-you-need-to-know-when-booking-hayman-island-resort-in-australia-for-your-destination-wedding (anchor must not name the resort, e.g. 'our Whitsundays island guide'); one line pointing mainland couples to /best-wedding-spots-in-byron-bay (anchor without 'best') and /au/venues-in-sydney. Season from the Bureau of Meteorology for a named Whitsundays station and its tropical cyclone season wording; legal line: Australian law applies and a notice of intended marriage is lodged at least one month before, linking /expert-advice/notice-of-intended-marriage-explained-step-by-step and /expert-advice/who-can-perform-a-marriage (both live), only as those pages' AGD facts state it.

Entry template for all 10, in this order: 'Why it suits a wedding' or 'The trade-off' (one honest paragraph, no venue or resort names); 'When to go' (seasons only as the official source states them, station and period named, Smartraveller cyclone line dated as at November 2026, linked at the claim, with fact markers); 'Getting married there' (legal or symbolic only from an official source, else exactly 'check with the destination's authorities', with the symbolic ceremony as the fallback; never a same-sex legal position beyond quoted law text); 'Questions for the venue' (two bullets); 'Our guide' (link where one exists; for no-guide entries omit the line entirely, no placeholder).

At-a-glance table in plain words: Destination | Region | Wet or cyclone season (as the source states it) | Getting married (legal route stated, or 'check with the destination's authorities') | Our guide (link or 'not yet'). Values must match the entries exactly. Then 'What to plan for a wedding in the Pacific' with short parts on cyclone season cover and a buffer day, the one-line legal note linking /destination-weddings/weddings-abroad-where-can-you-legally-get-married and /expert-advice/symbolic-ceremony (with the Smartraveller line that an overseas marriage cannot be registered in Australia but is in most cases recognised if valid where it took place, reusing wedding-in-crete fact_120 or notice-of-intended-marriage fact_20), and guests travelling from Australia as questions only. The single body Wedded Advisor line goes here: 'One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact from start to finish.' Also link /expert-advice/how-to-plan-a-destination-wedding, /destinations/oceania (if indexable), /magazine (UTM magnet) and the Wedded Concierge secondary CTA.

FAQ (4 to 6 questions), e.g. What are the most popular places in Oceania for a wedding abroad? When is cyclone season in the South Pacific? Can Australians get married legally in Fiji? Is Hawaii part of Oceania? Is a wedding in Tahiti legal or symbolic? Answers repeat entry facts only, no new claims. Then close 'Plan your Oceania wedding with Wedded Concierge': one Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments as your single point of contact, quotes in AUD, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins; closing CTA with the anchor 'Wedded Concierge'.

'Best', 'top', 'most beautiful', rankings or numbering implying order of merit (the Byron Bay link anchor must not say 'best')
Any temperature, rainfall or rain day figure not quoted from the named official source with station and period; any statistic other than sourced weather
Stating any marriage requirement, residency period, document or waiting time not quoted from an official source; any same-sex legal position beyond quoted law text
Softening or stretching cyclone, wet season or security wording beyond what Smartraveller or the met service says
Linking any internal guide from Vanuatu, New Caledonia, Tahiti and French Polynesia, the Cook Islands or Tonga (no guide of ours); no vendor or venue pages
Research talk ('we analysed', 'our research', search results); 'free' (including in anchors to the Australia magazine page); 'last dance'
Advisor claims about room blocks, Wedded Privileges, transfers, availability, who is on the ground, or phone lines
Flight times, routes, visa rules, holiday dates
Headings with colons, dashes or hyphens, or questions outside the FAQ; em dashes anywhere
Clichés the persona dislikes ('paradise', 'fairytale', 'dream day'); competitor wording or claims; US spelling
AI images of any real destination
